name: GHRP-2
used_for: A synthetic growth hormone secretagogue that acts on the ghrelin receptor. It has no FDA-approved product. It has been studied as a growth hormone stimulation test, and a 2013 Japanese study states that a GHRP-2 test is a recommended alternative for diagnosing adult growth hormone deficiency in Japan. It is promoted online for muscle, fat loss and recovery, which has not been shown in controlled human trials found for this entry. FDA lists it as a bulk substance that may present significant safety risks for compounding.

entries.text: Subcutaneous infusion of 1 microgram per kg per hour for 270 minutes, versus saline, before a meal.
Oral 900 micrograms per kg twice daily for 12 months.
entries.population: Ten prepubertal children with growth hormone deficiency

entries.text: Single intravenous doses of 1 and 2 micrograms per kg.
entries.population: Six healthy young adults and six elderly adults (2 micrograms per kg)

internet_entries.text: An affiliate-linked peptide site says the usual range is 100 to 300 mcg per injection, 1 to 3 times daily, with tiers of 100 mcg twice daily for beginners up to 150 to 200 mcg three times daily for advanced users.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: The Peptidepedia website says GHRP-2 is taken on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before eating or 2 or more hours after a meal, with the pre-bed injection emphasized, and that a mixed vial is refrigerated and used within 3 to 4 weeks, not frozen.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: The Peptidepedia website says GHRP-2 is injected subcutaneously into abdominal fat, thigh or deltoid with sites rotated, that the powder is dissolved with bacteriostatic water by swirling, never shaking, and that vials are kept in the original packaging or foil away from light.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: Subcutaneous GHRP-2 infusion increased food intake at a buffet meal by about 36% in seven healthy men.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Seven of ten children with growth hormone deficiency given oral GHRP-2 for 12 months reported a significant increase in appetite during the first 6 months; the change in BMI was not significant.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Intravenous GHRP-2 raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol levels in healthy adults, in addition to growth hormone.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: FDA lists GHRP-2 among bulk drug substances for compounding that may present significant safety risks, stating it may pose risk for immunogenicity due to the potential for aggregation and peptide-related impurities.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A peptide wiki guide calls GHRP-2 the most potent classic growth hormone-releasing peptide with less hunger than GHRP-6, lists beginner to advanced dosing protocols and stacking with CJC-1295, and states it is not FDA-approved in the US.

A comparison article says GHRP-2 causes much less hunger than GHRP-6 but raises cortisol and prolactin more, that both are usually stacked with CJC-1295, and that neither is FDA-approved so all human use is off-label.

research.summary: Crossover study of GHRP-2 infusion versus saline in seven lean healthy men, followed by a buffet meal (J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Participants ate about 36% more during the GHRP-2 infusion and growth hormone rose strongly. Very small study, but it confirms an appetite effect.

research.summary: Ten children with growth hormone deficiency took oral GHRP-2 for 12 months (J Pediatr Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Seven of ten reported more appetite during the first six months, but body mass index did not change significantly. No control group.

research.summary: Comparison of intravenous GHRP-2 and hexarelin with GHRH in six young and six elderly healthy people (Peptides).
research.finding: GHRP-2 produced a strong growth hormone response, larger than GHRH, but also raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol.

research.summary: Report of chronic GHRP-2, GHRH or combined administration for 7 to 30 days in healthy men and women (J Pediatr Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Chronic dosing changed how the growth hormone response behaved, and whether the response weakened (desensitized) depended partly on dose and frequency. The abstract gives no clinical outcome data.

research.summary: 71 Japanese adults with pituitary tumors underwent insulin, arginine and GHRP-2 stimulation tests (Endocr J).
research.finding: The GHRP-2 test gave higher peak growth hormone than the insulin test and was judged an acceptable alternative for diagnosing severe adult growth hormone deficiency. This is diagnostic testing, not therapy.

research.summary: FDA page on bulk drug substances for compounding that may present significant safety risks (content current as of 22 April 2026, fetched 2026-09-30).
research.finding: GHRP-2 (injectable and nasal routes) is listed under category 2 for 503B, added 29 September 2023. FDA cites immunogenicity risk and says it is aware of reports of serious adverse events in patients who received GHRP-2, including increased insulin requirement, death of critically ill study subjects, infection and pancreatitis, though causality has not been established.

research.summary: FDA warning letter to a compounding pharmacy (1 April 2020), fetched 2026-09-30.
research.finding: The letter lists GHRP-2 among substances the pharmacy compounded and says products made from them were not eligible for the section 503A exemptions; it notes GHRP-2 was nominated without adequate support for FDA to evaluate it and that the pharmacy said it removed it from its formulary.

research.summary: Study in 7 healthy young adults of how an oral glucose load and arginine change the growth hormone response to injected GHRH (Ghigo et al., Metabolism).
research.finding: Oral glucose beforehand lowered the GH peak after GHRH from 11.6 to 7.4 micrograms per liter; the authors suggest, from indirect evidence, that glucose acts by raising hypothalamic somatostatin.

research.summary: Frequent-sampling study of 24-hour growth hormone secretion in 6 healthy men on a fed day and on days 1 and 5 of a 5-day fast (Ho et al., J Clin Invest).
research.finding: Fasting increased growth hormone secretion and amplified its daily rhythms compared with the fed day.

research.summary: Study of growth hormone secretion in healthy men in relation to sleep and time of day, using deconvolution of frequent blood samples (Van Cauter et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: A GH pulse began within 30 minutes of sleep onset in every profile with normal sleep, and about 70% of pulses during sleep were tied to slow-wave sleep.

research.summary: Uncontrolled study of intranasal GHRP-2 (5 to 15 micrograms per kg, twice a day for 3 months, then three times a day) in 15 children with short stature, 6 of them followed for 18 to 24 months (Pihoker et al., J Endocrinol).
research.finding: Height velocity rose from 3.7 to 6.1 cm per year at 6 months and stayed at 6.0 cm per year at 18 to 24 months. Acute GH responses to GHRP-2 did not change significantly, and the spray was well tolerated. There was no control group.

research.summary: Case report of one woman with a 20-year history of anorexia nervosa given intranasal GHRP-2 before every meal for 1 year (Haruta et al., J Cachexia Sarcopenia Muscle).
research.finding: GHRP-2 increased hunger and food intake, and her body weight rose by 6.7 kg (from 21.1 to 27.8 kg) over 14 months. The authors observed no obvious side effects. One patient, no control.

dose.summary: Not approved. Studies used IV or infusion doses of 1 to 2 mcg per kg, a nasal spray in children, or a high oral dose in children. Online sources describe 100 to 300 mcg injected per dose, which has not been studied in trials.

items.text: Peptidepedia says a single 100 mcg dose at bedtime is a typical starting point and that the usual range is 100 to 300 mcg per injection. It says GHRP-2 is most often stacked with CJC-1295, a growth hormone releasing hormone (GHRH) analog, and states it is not FDA-approved.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Nerds says GHRP-2 is dosed at 100 to 300 mcg per subcutaneous injection and is almost always stacked with a GHRH analog such as CJC-1295. It states that neither GHRP-2 nor GHRP-6 is FDA-approved, so all human use is off-label.
items.label: internet

timing.summary: No study tested timing. The body's own growth hormone (GH) peaks after falling asleep, and online sources favor a pre-bed dose, though this has not been tested with GHRP-2.

items.text: The body's own largest GH pulse comes shortly after falling asleep. This is natural GH, not GHRP-2.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says the pre-bed injection is considered most important because it amplifies the natural nighttime GH surge.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Nerds says common injection times are before a workout, before sleep and mid-day while fasted.
items.label: internet

items.text: An affiliate-linked peptide site (PeptideWiki) says injections are timed on waking before breakfast, optionally 2 to 3 hours after lunch, and 30 to 60 minutes before sleep.
items.label: internet

fasting.summary: No study tested GHRP-2 with meals. Glucose blunted GH release in a GHRH study and fasting raised natural GH, and online sources say to inject on an empty stomach.

items.text: In healthy adults, a glucose drink lowered the GH response to injected GHRH by about a third. GHRP-2 works through a different receptor (ghrelin), and meals have not been tested with it.
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy men, fasting increased the body's own GH secretion compared with a fed day.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says GHRP-2 is taken on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before eating or 2 or more hours after a meal.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Nerds says to inject fasted or 2 or more hours after a meal to avoid insulin-driven blunting of the GH response.
items.label: internet

items.text: An affiliate-linked peptide site (PeptideWiki) says to fast at least 2 hours before an injection and wait 20 to 30 minutes before eating, and calls this non-negotiable.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: Children in studies took it by mouth twice daily or by nasal spray two to three times daily for months. Online sources describe 1 to 3 injections a day, and some add days off each week, which has not been studied.

cycle_length.summary: Children used it for up to 12 to 24 months without loss of response in small uncontrolled studies, and a 7 to 30 day report said desensitization depended on dose and frequency. Online sources describe 8 to 12 weeks on and 4 to 8 weeks off, and no study tested on and off cycles or what happens after stopping.

storage_and_handling.summary: No official guidance. Online sources describe freezing or refrigerating the powder, mixing with bacteriostatic water by swirling, refrigerating the mixed vial for 3 to 4 weeks, and rotating injection sites.

items.text: Peptidepedia says unmixed powder is stored frozen at minus 20 degrees C for long-term stability or refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees C for shorter periods, and that vials are kept in the original box or wrapped in foil away from light.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptidepedia says a mixed vial is refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees C and used within 3 to 4 weeks, and that reconstituted peptide should never be frozen.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptidepedia says the powder is dissolved with bacteriostatic water by swirling gently, never shaking.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptidepedia says GHRP-2 is injected under the skin into abdominal fat, the thigh or the deltoid, with sites rotated to prevent lipodystrophy.
items.label: internet

items.text: An affiliate-linked peptide site (PeptideWiki) says a mixed vial is refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees C and used within 28 to 30 days.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: GHRP-2 is a synthetic agonist of the ghrelin receptor and releases growth hormone, but in people it also raises prolactin, ACTH and cortisol. Online sources describe the cell signaling in more detail.

items.text: GHRP-2 is a synthetic agonist of ghrelin, which binds the GH secretagogue receptor, and like ghrelin it increased food intake in seven healthy men.
items.label: research

items.text: Intravenous GHRP-2 produced a strong GH response, larger than GHRH, but also raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says GHRP-2 activates Gq/11 signaling and phospholipase C, which triggers release of GH granules, and calls it the most potent classic growth hormone-releasing peptide by peak GH output.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: Strong GH release, which is how it is used as a diagnostic test in Japan. Small uncontrolled studies suggest faster growth in short children and weight gain in one patient. No controlled trial tested muscle, fat loss or recovery.

items.text: A GHRP-2 test gave higher peak GH than the insulin test in 71 Japanese adults with pituitary tumors and was judged an acceptable alternative for diagnosing severe adult growth hormone deficiency. This is diagnostic testing, not therapy.
items.label: research

items.text: In 15 children with short stature given intranasal GHRP-2, height velocity rose from 3.7 to 6.1 cm per year at 6 months. There was no control group.
items.label: research

items.text: One patient with anorexia nervosa gained 6.7 kg over 14 months on intranasal GHRP-2 before meals. This is a single case report.
items.label: research

items.text: Participants ate about 36% more during the GHRP-2 infusion and GH rose strongly. Very small study, but it confirms an appetite effect.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Hunger
side_effect_groups.summary: GHRP-2 raised appetite in small studies. Online sources say it causes less hunger than GHRP-6.

items.text: Subcutaneous GHRP-2 infusion increased food intake at a buffet meal by about 36% in seven healthy men.
items.label: research

items.text: Seven of ten children with growth hormone deficiency given oral GHRP-2 for 12 months reported a significant increase in appetite during the first 6 months; the change in body mass index was not significant.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says GHRP-2 has less appetite stimulation than GHRP-6, which it says triggers robust hunger. It calls the appetite effect moderate.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Nerds says GHRP-2 produces significantly less hunger than GHRP-6, with mild to negligible hunger effects.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Hormone effects
side_effect_groups.summary: GHRP-2 raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol along with growth hormone. One online source says it does this more than GHRP-6.

items.text: Intravenous GHRP-2 raised prolactin, ACTH and cortisol levels in healthy adults, in addition to growth hormone.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Nerds says GHRP-2 raises cortisol and prolactin more than GHRP-6 does.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: In trials
side_effect_groups.summary: Nasal GHRP-2 was described as well tolerated in small uncontrolled studies. No controlled long-term safety data were found.

items.text: Intranasal GHRP-2 was described as well tolerated in 15 children with short stature followed for 6 months or longer, in a study with no control group.
items.label: research

items.text: The authors of a one-patient report of one year of intranasal GHRP-2 observed no obvious side effects.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Online reports
side_effect_groups.summary: Online sources list flushing, drowsiness, water retention, headaches, tingling and injection site reactions. These lists cite no trial data.

items.text: Peptidepedia lists increased appetite, flushing, transient drowsiness and mild water retention as side effects.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Nerds lists water retention, injection site reactions, headaches and tingling or numbness as common effects.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Regulator warning
side_effect_groups.summary: FDA lists compounded GHRP-2 as a possible safety risk and reports serious adverse events in patients, with causality not established.

items.text: FDA lists GHRP-2 among bulk drug substances for compounding that may present significant safety risks, stating it may pose risk for immunogenicity due to the potential for aggregation and peptide-related impurities.
items.label: research
